prompt:
I need the front end for Cratehold. A hosted private container registry for small engineering teams that keeps their images, tags and vulnerability scan results in one place.

Who's using it: Noor Haddad, one of two backend engineers at an 8-person company that sells scheduling software to veterinary clinics. She handles infrastructure part-time on top of feature work.

What they're doing right now: A critical vulnerability was announced this morning in a widely used base image's OpenSSL package. Noor has to go through everything the team has pushed, narrow it down to the images built on the affected base, see which of those are actually deployed or recently pulled, and open the worst one to check its build details before she messages the team about what needs rebuilding today.

What's in the system at this point: 38 repositories, 1,240 tags, 61 GB total. Example repos: 'api-gateway' (212 tags, latest 3 hours ago), 'appointment-worker', 'sms-reminders', 'pdf-invoices', 'legacy-php-portal' (last push 14 months ago). Each tag has a digest, size (48 MB–1.3 GB), base image (e.g., debian:12-slim, alpine:3.19, node:20-bookworm), push date, pushed-by (Noor, Sam, CI bot), last pulled, environment label (prod, staging, none), and scan results by severity. The new CVE-2026-41187 (critical) affects images based on debian:12 built before Nov 14: 17 tags across 9 repos, 4 of them labeled prod. Retention policy: untagged images are deleted after 30 days.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
